journeys.title: 10 Minutes with Jesus
journeys.description: A short, guided journey to help you connect with Jesus in the middle of your everyday life.

journeys.title: Who Is God?
journeys.description: A 7-day introduction to knowing Jesus — who he is, what he did, and how to follow him.

journeys.title: The Road to Emmaus
journeys.subtitle: A 3-day walk through Luke 24
journeys.description: Walk the road to Emmaus alongside the two disciples who did not recognise Jesus — and discover how he opens the Scriptures, meets us in our grief, and reveals himself in the breaking of bread.

steps.title: Come and See
steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning.

I'm glad you're here.

You don't need to know everything today.

You simply need to take one more step with Jesus.
steps.teaching_content:
Two ordinary men heard John the Baptist speak about Jesus.

Curious, they began to follow Him.

Jesus turned and asked them,

"What are you seeking?"

It wasn't because He didn't know.

It was because they needed to know.

That question still matters today.

Why are you here?

Are you looking for hope?

Peace?

Forgiveness?

A fresh start?

Or are you simply curious about Jesus?

Whatever brought you here...

Jesus welcomes honest seekers.

He doesn't ask you to have all the answers before you come to Him.

He simply invites you to begin walking with Him.

Today isn't about completing a lesson.

It's about taking your first step towards knowing Jesus.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for welcoming people who are still searching.

Thank You for inviting me to come to You just as I am.

Help me to know You a little better today and to keep taking one step at a time.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
If you have a few quiet moments today, read the rest of John chapter 1.

As you read, ask yourself one simple question:

What does this teach me about Jesus?

Don't worry if you don't understand everything.

Just keep looking at Him.

steps.title: Jesus Knows Your Name
steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm glad you're back.

Yesterday, Jesus invited you to come and see.

Today, you'll discover something even more personal.

He already knows you.
steps.teaching_content:
Andrew had only just met Jesus.

Before long, he brought his brother Simon to meet Him too.

Jesus looked at Simon and immediately called him by name.

Then He gave him a new name.

Peter.

Jesus wasn't simply identifying him.

He was revealing who Simon could become.

That's still how Jesus works today.

He knows your past.

He knows your struggles.

He knows your fears.

He also knows the person He is shaping you to become.

You may only see your weaknesses.

Jesus sees your future.

He doesn't wait until you've changed before calling you.

He calls you first...

and then begins changing you.

Take a quiet moment to thank Him for knowing you completely—and loving you anyway.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that You know me completely.

Nothing about my life is hidden from You.

Thank You for loving me as I am, while patiently shaping me into the person You created me to be.

Help me trust the work You are doing in my life, even when I cannot yet see it.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
If you have a few quiet moments today,

as you go through John 1, look for what Jesus sees in the people He calls.

Then ask yourself:

What might Jesus be shaping in me?

Don't worry if you don't have all the answers.

Keep walking with Him.

steps.title: Follow Me
steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm grateful you're walking with Jesus again today.

Over the last two days you've discovered that Jesus welcomes you and knows you personally.

Today, He extends an invitation.

Not just to believe something about Him...

but to follow Him.
steps.teaching_content:
When Jesus found Philip, He didn't give him a long explanation.

He simply said,

"Follow Me."

Those two words changed Philip's life forever.

Following Jesus isn't about having every question answered before taking the first step.

It's about trusting the One who is leading you.

Philip didn't keep the invitation to himself.

He immediately found Nathanael and shared the good news with him.

Nathanael wasn't convinced.

He had questions.

He even doubted whether anything good could come from Nazareth.

Philip didn't argue.

He simply said,

"Come and see."

That's often the best response we can give.

We don't have to know everything.

We don't have to win every debate.

We simply keep following Jesus and invite others to discover Him for themselves.

Jesus is patient with honest questions.

He welcomes people who are willing to come and see.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for inviting me to follow You.

Help me trust You even when I don't have every answer.

Teach me to take the next step in faith and to gently point others towards You.

May my life make people curious about Jesus.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
As you go through today, ask yourself one simple question:

"What would following Jesus look like in this situation?"

Whether you're at home, at work, at school or with friends, let that question guide one decision today.

Remember...

Following Jesus happens one step at a time.

steps.title: Jesus Sees You
steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

I'm thankful you've come back today.

Sometimes we wonder if anyone really understands us.

Today, we'll meet a man who discovered that Jesus saw him long before they ever met.
steps.teaching_content:
When Nathanael approached Jesus, he expected to meet a stranger.

Instead, Jesus spoke as someone who already knew him.

Before Nathanael had taken a single step towards Jesus, Jesus had already seen him sitting under the fig tree.

We aren't told why Nathanael was there.

Perhaps he was praying.

Perhaps he was reading Scripture.

Perhaps he was simply alone with his thoughts.

Whatever happened beneath that tree, it mattered enough that Jesus mentioned it.

That changed everything.

The same Jesus sees you today.

He sees the parts of your life that nobody else notices.

He sees your joys.

He sees your disappointments.

He sees your prayers that nobody has heard.

He sees your quiet acts of faithfulness.

Nothing about your life escapes His attention.

You never have to fight for His attention.

You already have it.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that nothing in my life is hidden from You.

Thank You for seeing me completely and loving me faithfully.

Help me remember that even when I feel unnoticed by others, I am always known and seen by You.

Teach me to trust Your presence every day.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few quiet moments today and remember one time when God faithfully cared for you.

Thank Him for it.

Then ask Him to help you notice His presence again today, even in ordinary moments.

He is nearer than you think.

steps.title: Jesus Brings New Life
steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

It's good to be walking with you again today.

Over the last few days, we've been discovering who Jesus is.

Today, we'll see what happens when He steps into an ordinary situation.
steps.teaching_content:
A wedding should have been filled with celebration.

Instead, the hosts faced embarrassment.

The wine had run out.

For the families involved, this wasn't a small inconvenience. It was a moment of disappointment and shame.

Nobody expected Jesus to solve the problem.

Yet He quietly stepped into the situation and changed everything.

The ordinary jars of water became the finest wine.

That's the first miracle John records, and it's no accident.

From the very beginning, Jesus shows us that He brings new life where people have run out.

Perhaps today you've run out too.

Maybe you've run out of hope.

Or strength.

Or peace.

Or joy.

Jesus still specialises in bringing new life to places that seem empty.

He doesn't always work the way we expect.

But He is always able to do far more than we can imagine.

Nothing is beyond His power.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You that You bring new life into places that feel empty.

Where I have run out of hope, fill me with Your peace.

Where I feel weak, strengthen me.

Help me trust that nothing is impossible for You.

Teach me to bring every part of my life to You, knowing that You are able to transform it.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few moments today to think about one area of your life where you need Jesus to work.

Tell Him honestly.

You don't need impressive words.

Simply place that situation into His hands and trust Him with it.

He is still the God who brings new life.

steps.title: Jesus Changes What Matters

content.closingText: Tomorrow we'll begin a new stage of our journey together as we discover why Jesus came.

steps.mentor_intro:
Good morning, {{first_name}}.

It's good to spend this time with Jesus again.

Over the last few days you've discovered who Jesus is.

Today we'll discover something else.

Where Jesus is welcomed, lives begin to change.
steps.teaching_content:
When Jesus entered the temple, He didn't see what everyone else saw.

People saw a busy place of worship.

Jesus saw a place that had lost its purpose.

The temple had become filled with noise, business and distraction, while the worship of God had been pushed into the background.

Jesus wasn't angry because people were buying and selling.

He was passionate because His Father's House had become something it was never meant to be.

As we follow Jesus, He gently begins doing the same work in our lives.

He lovingly shows us attitudes that need changing.

Habits that hold us back.

Priorities that have quietly taken God's place.

This isn't about making us feel guilty.

It's about making room for something better.

Jesus never removes something good without offering something greater.

The closer we walk with Him, the more our lives begin to reflect what matters most.
steps.prayer:
Lord,

Thank You for loving me enough to change me.

Help me recognise the areas of my life where You want to do Your work.

Give me the humility to trust You, even when change feels uncomfortable.

Teach me to love what You love and to place You at the very centre of my life.

Amen.
steps.todays_action:
Take a few quiet moments today and ask yourself:

"Is there anything that's becoming more important to me than Jesus?"

Don't be afraid of the answer.

Simply place that area before Him and ask Him to shape your heart.

Real change begins when we trust Him.

steps.title: Born Again
steps.mentor_intro: Good morning. It's good to spend this time with Jesus again. Today we're going to discover why following Jesus is more than becoming a better person—it is receiving a brand new life.
steps.teaching_content:
Nicodemus was a respected religious leader. He knew the Scriptures, lived a moral life and sincerely wanted to understand Jesus. Yet Jesus told him something surprising: "You must be born again."

Jesus wasn't saying that we simply need to try harder or become more religious. He was teaching that real life with God begins when He changes us from the inside out. It's a work of God's Spirit, not something we can achieve by our own efforts.

Many people spend years trying to improve themselves, hoping they'll eventually be good enough for God. But the gospel is not about earning God's acceptance. It's about receiving the new life that Jesus freely offers through faith in Him.

When you trust Jesus, He doesn't just forgive your past—He begins transforming your heart, your desires and the direction of your life. Growth takes time, but the journey begins with new life that only He can give.

If you've already placed your trust in Jesus, thank Him for making you new. If you're still exploring who Jesus is, know that His invitation is open to you today.
steps.prayer: Father, thank You for the new life You offer through Jesus Christ. I know I cannot save myself or change my own heart. Please continue Your work in me, making me more like Jesus each day. Help me to trust You and follow wherever You lead. Amen.
steps.todays_action: Spend a few minutes thanking God for one way He has already changed your life. If you're still seeking Him, simply pray, "Jesus, help me to know You and understand what it means to be born again."

steps.title: God Wants You to Know Him
Walking in the Dark
steps.teaching_content:
Two disciples were walking away from Jerusalem — away from hope. Cleopas and his companion had seen Jesus crucified, and now the tomb was empty. They had heard reports of resurrection, but it all seemed like an idle tale.

Jesus joined them on the road. He walked beside them. He asked them questions. He listened. And they did not recognise him.

Sometimes our grief or confusion is so great that we walk right past the presence of Jesus. He is with us on the road even when we cannot see him. He does not abandon us in our confusion — he enters it.
steps.reflection_question: When have you found yourself walking away from hope? What did God's presence look like in that season, even if you did not recognise it at the time?
steps.prayer: Lord Jesus, open my eyes to see you walking beside me today — even in the places that feel most confusing or broken. Amen.
steps.todays_action: Take a short walk today. As you walk, bring one unanswered question or grief to God and simply tell him where you are.

steps.title: When Scripture Burns
steps.teaching_content:
Jesus, still unrecognised, turned to the two disciples and did something extraordinary: he opened the Scriptures. Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.

The Bible was not a collection of moral lessons or historical records — it was a story, and Jesus was its centre. Every promise, every sacrifice, every rescue was pointing forward to this moment.

The disciples later said their hearts burned within them as he spoke. That burning is the Holy Spirit at work, making Scripture come alive.
steps.reflection_question: Which part of the Bible feels most alive to you at the moment — and which part feels most distant? Bring both to God today.
steps.prayer: Open the Scriptures to me, Lord. Let my heart burn as yours did on the road. Show me how everything points to you. Amen.
steps.todays_action: Read Luke 24:13-35 in full today. Notice every time the disciples understanding shifts. What changes for them — and why?

steps.title: Known in the Breaking
steps.teaching_content:
They reached the village. Jesus acted as though he were going further. But they urged him: stay with us, for it is nearly evening. And he went in to stay with them.

At table, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. And their eyes were opened. They recognised him — and he vanished from their sight.

Jesus is known in the breaking. In the ordinary act of sharing bread, in the moment of communion, in the everyday table of life — he reveals himself. And the moment they recognised him, they immediately got up and returned to Jerusalem. Encountering the risen Jesus changes the direction of your life.
steps.reflection_question: Where has Jesus made himself known to you through something ordinary — a meal, a conversation, a moment you almost missed?
steps.prayer: Thank you, Jesus, that you reveal yourself in the breaking. Open my eyes to recognise you in the everyday moments of my life. Amen.
steps.todays_action: Share a meal with someone today — family, a friend, a neighbour — and pray before you eat, asking God to make himself known at your table.
